utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-0 IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Kyle Wood, Aditya Menon, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, and good morning to everybody in the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson representing General Delic, with our legal assistants, Lana Deljkic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, may I remind you, you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Judge, any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you mentioned in your evidence that on the 1st of June, 1993, you went to Zapode, where you joined a group of Arabs. Did that group have a name?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did it have a name at any other time?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, that group became the El Mujahed Detachment, which was part of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to explain what you mean by saying it was "part of the BiH Army"?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was part of the army, by formation, by establishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "By formation, by establishment," are you able to elaborate a little bit more? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given our status as a detachment, and we belonged to the 3rd Corps of the BiH Army. We were part of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that sometime during your operations, I think from Zapode going down, you came across some two or three bodies of dead people. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not three; one or two, that's what I said. I'm sure that there were two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who killed these people?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly who killed them. In any case, during the operation in the morning, whoever was breaking through the line, this happened in the trench, midline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I understand that answer.

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: When you are making an attempt to break through the line, the enemy waits in the trenches. As you launch the attack, you move towards the trenches. Those who do not flee before you reach the trenches get killed if they don't escape first before you reach those trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you, by any chance, know the ethnicity of these victims?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The line was facing the Croats. They were wearing uniforms, they were on the Croat side, and most probably they were Croats. I did not inspect any ID papers, but I would suspect they were Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How do you determine that they were on the Croat side?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where the trenches were, and the bodies were lying strewn on the edge of the trench. That's where I saw them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You just said they were wearing a uniform. Are you able to tell what uniform they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms; the complete uniform with boots, the anorak, and the camouflage trousers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I'm trying to find out is: Were you able to identify whose army that uniform belonged to? Was it the HVO, was it the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or was it the VRS? What was it, the uniform?

utterances.speaker: SABIN ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably the HVO. I passed by that trench, and I just threw a glance. I did not have the time to look for any insignia. I did not see any insignia. I did not look for insignia because I didn't have the time to do that. Do you see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That concludes my questions. Any re-examination arising from the questions by the Bench, Mr. Wood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, this brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for taking time off to come and testify for the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may leave. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Registry has indicated that we need to take a short break to prepare the courtroom for the next witness. You said 20 minutes? Twenty minutes. We'll break for 20 minutes and come back in 20 minutes' time. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to confirm, do we go into private or closed session or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's best if we begin in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Before we move into private session, I guess I can say this with the witness present here. Is it possible to ask the Defence for an expedited response to the 73 bis (F) motion so that hopefully a decision could be rendered before the recess? I guess it is in the interests of everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We received the motion yesterday. We're working on it. We'll be able to forward a response in the next few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Thank you. I know you've got two weeks, but just so that we can render a decision before recess.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Indeed, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. That being the case, then can we move into private session? Can we make the declaration first before we move into private?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated, sir. All right. May the Chamber now move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, can you please tell the Trial Chamber when the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina began, as far as you are aware?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In spring 2002 -- I'm sorry, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, at that time, spring 1992, when the war began in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I was living in Sanski Most. However, I was at school in Ljubljana in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, after the war began, did you join any military force or armed force?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: After the war began, I returned from Slovenia and I arrived in Travnik, and I joined a unit of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber, sir, what steps you took in travelling from Slovenia to Travnik, where you joined a unit of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In Slovenia, there were a lot of people from my town. When the war started, we did not know anything about our families. We sought ways to return to Bosnia. I learned in Zagreb that there was a place where our people were gathering. After a certain while, I arrived in Zagreb, that is. I joined a group on its way to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, sir, just so that we all understand, you travelled from Ljubljana to Zagreb, and from Zagreb to Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, approximately when you arrived in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In late June or early July. I can't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And the year, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, when you arrived in Travnik, can you tell the Trial Chamber to what location in Travnik you went?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We arrived at the former JNA barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You told us a few moments ago, sir, that you joined a unit of volunteers. Did that unit of volunteers have a name at the time you joined in late June, early July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, PW-2, to what armed force or military force the 1st Krajina Battalion was a part?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was the Territorial Defence at the time, since the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had not been formed yet. So I believe it was the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, approximately when the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was formed?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know that there were transformation processes ongoing. Perhaps at the end of 1992, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was formed out of the Territorial Defence, but it happened gradually.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At the time you joined the 1st Krajina Battalion, PW-2, in late June or early July of 1992, do you know who the commander of that battalion was?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Osman Omanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber, PW-2, why a unit with the name "1st Krajina Battalion" was formed in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We came from Slovenia in order to defend our families. We organised that unit ourselves, as fighters.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were the members of the 1st Krajina Battalion from the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Most of them were.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber what the Krajina is?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The Krajina is the northwestern part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was under a total blockade in relation to the other parts of the country.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is Travnik located in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: That region gravitates toward the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, PW-2, that the members of the 1st Krajina Battalion were refugees from the Krajina who joined this unit in order to fight?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: First off, there were us volunteers who had been working or schooling in Slovenia. Later on, refugees from other parts of the country started joining us.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, how long did you remain a member of the 1st Krajina Battalion based in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: A month and a half, roughly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During the time period that you were with the 1st Krajina Battalion, where was the headquarters of that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I believe it was in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, again, sir, for the benefit of the record and the Trial Chamber, when you say "the barracks," can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The barracks we arrived at, the JNA barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And at the time, PW-2, when you arrived at the JNA barracks in Travnik, was the JNA still at that barracks?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Other than the 1st Krajina Battalion, were there any other military units located at the former JNA barracks in Travnik, to the best of your recollection or knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In one part of the barracks, there was one HVO unit.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During the time period, sir, that you were with the 1st Krajina Battalion, did you engage in any combat operations with that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just interrupt for a while. Just one question, Mr. Mundis. This former JNA barracks, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber in what areas you engaged in combat operations while you were a member of the 1st Krajina Battalion from late June, early July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It was the area of Turbe in the direction of Donji Vakuf or Jajce.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, during the one and a half month period that you were with the 1st Krajina Battalion, did you see or encounter any foreign fighters; that is, fighters from outside Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No, not at the lines.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at the time period you were with the 1st Krajina Battalion, see any foreign fighters in any locations other than the front lines?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: When I returned from the front lines for a rest at the Travnik barracks, I saw foreigners coming once.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, when you say you "saw foreigners coming once," coming to where? At what location did you see these foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I saw them coming to the JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, approximately, how many foreign fighters you saw coming to the JNA barracks on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: One car.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that you were a member of the 1st Krajina Battalion for one and a half months. After that period, that is, after you served with the 1st Krajina Battalion, did you join any other military unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate date, sir, that you joined this other military unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In late August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, could I just interrupt to ask the witness when he saw the foreign fighters at the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them at the time when I was absent from the lines. We had a rotation of shifts, because the 1st Krajina Battalion did not have enough weapons. We replaced each other at the front lines. As I returned to the barracks for my first rest, I saw a car full of foreigners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps some 15 to 20 days before I joined the other unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And that was sometime in August 1993; is that correct -- 1992? Do you remember the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1992. Possibly in August, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Possibly in August 1992, you saw for the first time the foreign fighters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, this unit that you joined in late August 1992, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The Muslim Forces of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what steps, if any, you took in leaving the 1st Krajina Battalion and joining the Muslim Forces of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We had very small amounts of weapons in the 1st Krajina Battalion. I thought that I would have to wait for a long time before I get my weapons back, once I leave them at the front lines. And an individual approached me and invited me to join the Muslim Forces, as they had plenty of weapons. There were also Krajina fighters among them, and I accepted the offer.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In leaving the 1st Krajina Battalion, Witness PW-2, did you consult with your commander, or fill out any paperwork, or take any official steps such as those to leave the 1st Krajina Battalion and join the Muslim Forces of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, who the commander was of the Travnik Muslim Forces at the time you joined that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. There were several individuals there. When I first went to the front lines with the Muslim Forces, the commander was Asim Koricic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, the names of any other leaders of the Travnik Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: When I came to town, I knew of Ahmed Adilovic. There were some other individuals at the headquarters, Semir Terzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, could we just ask the witness to explain briefly to us why he left the Krajina Brigade and joined the Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Krajina unit was poorly furnished with weapons. We weren't able to do what we had come to do there in the first place, and whoever wanted could join the other unit because we shared the same goal, and there were other units that were better equipped with weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, when you say "we shared the same goal," can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We all shared the goal of defending our country against those who were attacking us.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, again, PW-2, can you tell the Trial Chamber who was attacking you at that time that you were with the Muslim Forces of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The Serb forces, the Serbs therefore.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, a few moments ago you mentioned the name "Ahmed Adilovic." Do you know what role Mr. Adilovic played in the Muslim Forces of Travnik during the time that you were with that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: He was among the Command Staff. They called him "Emir," but I can't tell exactly. He was one of the main people there of the people in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-2, whether Mr. Adilovic had responsibilities concerning religious affairs within the unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes, among other things.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You also mentioned, sir, the name "Semir Terzic." Do you know what responsibilities Mr. Terzic had within the Travnik Muslim Forces at the time you were with that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: As far as the group of soldiers that I was part of, he was in charge of training, and he was probably in charge of some other duties as well.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, other than Asim Koricic, Semir Terzic, and Ahmed Adilovic, do you remember any of the other leaders of the Travnik Muslim Forces during the time period you were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: There was a former JNA officer. People refer to him as "Major Tara," and I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, how long did you remain a member of the Muslim Forces of Travnik after joining that unit in late August 1992?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I was there for quite a while, even at the time when the unit was transformed into a new formation.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: We'll go into that transformation in a few moments, sir, but do you recall the approximate date that this transformation into a new formation occurred?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It was wintertime. It may have been the end of 1992. It may have been the end of -- the beginning of 1993. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I'd like to focus your attention, sir, on the period from late August 1992, when you joined the Travnik Muslim Forces, until this period at the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993, when the unit was transformed. During that time period from late August 1992 until the transformation, can you describe how the Travnik Muslim Forces were organised?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: They were organised in the same way as the other units were, as a military structure, although there were some differences.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I would ask you, PW-2, if you could explain how the unit was structured and also how it was different from other military units.

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can't explain the structure, really. As far as the differences go, people practiced religion to a greater degree than, say, in the Krajina unit.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During this time period, from late August 1992 until the unit was transformed at the end of 1992 or beginning of 1993, did you engage in any combat operations while serving as a member of the Travnik Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes. I participated in quite a few offensive activities.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe these offensive activities that you engaged in while a member of that unit, the locations and the approximate time periods of those offensive activities?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Until the end of 1992, we were oftentime present in the area toward Jajce, which is called Karaula. There were quite a few offensive activities there. The group which I was a part of first spent some time in Jajce, too.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Other than this area toward Jajce called Karaula, did you engage in any other combat actions at any other locations while engaged in the Travnik Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, we were present only in the areas of Karaula, Vlasic, and Jajce, but that's similar territory -- or rather, that's all close by. We were also present at Guca, near Donji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, a moment ago you mentioned a group, "the group which I was a part of." Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what this group that you were a part of was?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: This was one platoon of the Muslim Forces. We set out for Jajce. We numbered some 25 men. We were sent as assistants to the Krajina unit, as the Jajce area was under strong attacks.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Other than the Krajina unit and the Muslim Forces of Travnik, were there able to units of the ABiH that were in the Jajce area at that time?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: There was the HVO, too, in the Jajce area.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At this point in time, sir, autumn into early winter 1992, can you describe the relationship between the HVO and the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In 1992, I don't know exactly. We didn't have many contacts with them, and I didn't notice anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During this period, again, late 1992, was the BH Army and the HVO working together against the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Well, they were together at Jajce, although the units were separate, and I can't explain that, really.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: During the period in late 1992, was the BH Army and the HVO fighting each other in this area where you were located?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I know that there were some problems at Novi Travnik, but I don't know anything specific.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let's return, sir, to the issue of the Travnik Muslim Forces. Can you tell the Trial Chamber the composition of that unit during the time period that you were in it, in terms of where the people from that unit came from?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: During my stay in Travnik, while I was attending the training, there were only Bosniaks there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, sir, what time period are you referring to when you say "during my stay in Travnik, while I was attending the training"? What time period was that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Before I went to Karaula, to the field.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: With respect to the issue of Bosniaks, did that unit remain comprised only of Bosniaks after you returned from Karaula?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It was composed of Bosniaks, but in Karaula we were billeted in the village where foreigners were staying. So we were in the same place.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, where these foreigners came from?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Those were Arabs and Turks. There was several groups there. I don't know exactly. Different groups.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-2, if at any time while you were a member of the Travnik Muslim Forces, whether any foreign fighters joined that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were registered as members by establishment; but when we were in the field, we were together. We even participated in some actions together. When I say "together," I mean we were fighting together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown on e-court the document which has previously been marked PT or P01014.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And while this document is coming up, PW-2, do you recall the names of any other members of the Travnik Muslim Forces at the time period you were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember some names.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you please tell us those names, sir, of the people that you remember?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Number 1, Ahmed Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: If I could just interrupt, Witness, you're now looking at the document in front of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Which has been, again, marked P01014. And if you could, sir, as you've just done, indicate the number next to the names of the people that you recall serving with in this unit.

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Number 15, Faik Selman; number 16, Ramo Durmis; 22, Meho Begonovic.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Before we go to the next page in the Bosnia language, sir, earlier you mentioned Semir Terzic. Do you see his name on this list?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page, then, in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, again, sir, if you recognise any of the names of individuals that you served with in the Travnik Muslim Forces, please, indicate that.

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Muhammad Nevalic, 43; 48, Muharem Adilovic; number 49, Muris Ribo; number 60, Amir Puric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Scroll to the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65, Adem Siljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Sir, this document seems to be signed by someone who went by "Emir Redzic." Do you know who is or was?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. We referred to that person as "Major Tara." That could be him. It is quite possible, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please go back to the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe before you go to the first page, could we sort of get the witness to read for us, if he can, what's written on that stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Muslim Forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Muslim Forces of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the stamp looked like, but what I see here, the inscription, I mean, is "Muslim Forces."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could, again, go to the first page of this document, and if we could have the top half a little bit lower. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you see the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: 15 September 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, sir, were you a member of the Muslim Forces, Travnik, on that date?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask to briefly go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for a moment, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that in the English version, the date of the document is missing, which may be confusing the matter at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. I noticed that myself. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm asking my case manager if we can get that resubmitted for a revised version of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are now in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you know the name of the person within the Travnik Muslim Forces who was responsible for logistics or supply issues?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I believe that there were a few, a few people involved in that, because the supplies were obtained in various ways. As far as I can remember, one of them was Semir Terzic, but I'm sure that there were a few people involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would ask that this document, previously P01014, be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just ask the witness if his name appears on the list? He doesn't have to -- just "yes" or "no." I may have missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could go back into private session for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, I realise -- I'm aware of the fact that we had a break of 20 minutes a little earlier, but we're now confusing our schedule for the rest of the day. How much longer would you like to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could just go -- well, if it's convenient for the Trial Chamber, I'm certainly happy to stop at this point, if that would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber would like to stop at the point when it's convenient for Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour. If I could go perhaps another five or six minutes, perhaps about 20 to, and I think that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, PW-2, as reflected a few moments ago on page 21, line 14, you recognised one of the names on this list as being that of Ramo Durmis. Can you tell the Trial Chamber how it is that you came to know the person Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when he joined, but in any case he was the commander of a group in the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, PW-2, did you ever serve in the group that was commanded by Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I was for a while, I suppose. It changed frequently. We changed our affiliation quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, PW-2, whether Ramo Durmis had a nickname or whether he went by any pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: He liked to call himself "Abu Jihad."

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, PW-2, where Ramo Durmis came from?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Ramo Durmis was not from Travnik, I believe. I think he was from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now, immediately prior to the break, if the witness could be shown P02960. That's P02960.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And while that's coming up, Witness, do you know an individual by the name of Makteuf?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how you know this person and where he came from?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: On a couple of occasions, I saw him in Travnik, when I was in training at the Muslim Forces. I know that he was together with Semir Terzic and some people from the command, and that he provided some sort of logistical support.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, PW-2, where Mr. Makteuf came from?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I believe that he was from Iraq.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, PW-2, do you now see a document in front of you? I apologise for the poor quality of this document, but do you see a document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Again, sir, I would ask you if you could please look down this list and give us just the number of the person -- of any person whose name you recognise as being a member of the Muslim Forces.

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Number 1, number 4, number 5, number 18, 20, 31, 37, 42.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Okay. Before we go to the next page, sir, do you see on this list that after each first name there are the letters "Ibn"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what that means?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: This means "son." However, I find this document rather peculiar because I don't know this "Ibn." This wasn't actually used. It's an Arab word, and I don't know who put it there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page of this document. And before we continue with this exercise, I would ask that we go into private session for this part of the witness's testimony, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would tender P02960 into evidence and ask that that be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P02960 has been admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit 104.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This would be an appropriate spot for the first break -- the second break, actually, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've got to work out when we come back. We come back at, what, quarter past 11.00? Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that delay. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, I'm going to show you in just a moment a videotape. But before I do that, I'd like to ask you, sir: During the time period that you were with the Travnik Muslim Forces, were you aware of the location where that unit had its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The unit had its headquarters in the town itself close to the police station.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about this headquarters, what building or buildings it was located in?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I only know that it was downtown. It's just an ordinary building. There's nothing special to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now, Your Honours, that the witness be shown the video which has been marked P06001. And for the benefit of the transcript, we're beginning this videotape at the point eight minutes and 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to do this in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And before I show this tape to you, PW-2, I'm going to ask you if at any point in this tape you recognise anyone, if you can just say the word "stop" and we will pause the videotape. Similarly, I will ask you, sir, if you recognise the location where this videotape was taken, I would ask you similarly to indicate that by simply telling us where the location of the videotape is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I don't believe, Your Honours, it's necessary for the audio portion of this tape to be played; but if Your Honours would like the audio played, we can certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is an English version transcript associated with the tape. Perhaps we should just play the audio for the benefit of the accused and the Bosnian speakers who might be following the proceedings, so we will do that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But, again, sir, if you see anyone or recognise the location, simply say "stop," and we'll pause the videotape. Again, this is P06001, beginning at minute 8, 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is the late Major Tara. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have a video -- a photo capture of this portion of the tape which I would ask that the witness be shown, and if this could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, if you look at the photograph on the machine to your left, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The image is very poor.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Perhaps rather than looking at the screen, if you could actually look at the hard copy of the photograph on the machine to your left. That might be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It's still of very poor quality. I believe that I recognised him on the video, but this image is too blurred for me.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That's fine. We'll continue, then, with the videotape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I note, for the record, that the video is currently paused at 10 minutes, 2 seconds. Go ahead and continue the video, please.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, we're now at 10 minutes 36 seconds on the videotape P06001. Do you recognise anyone at this location of the tape?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can see that there's a foreigner here next to him. Interpreting for him is the Travnik Mufti.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you describe, sir, what the person you've indicated as the "Travnik Mufti" is wearing in this video at 10 minutes 36 seconds?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I believe he's wearing the religious robe.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what colour the religious robe that he's wearing is?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It's either grey or white. I can't tell exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Is the person you've identified as the "Travnik Mufti" holding anything in his hands?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We can continue, then, please, with the video.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Do you recognise this person who you've indicated is a foreigner?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask the videotape continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that this is the barracks where we were billeted when I had my training.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you know the name of this building that's in the background of this videotape?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: This was formerly a religious school, long before. It was then seized by the Communists and used for other purposes. After the war, it was turned into a religious school again. During the war, we used it as a barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Does this building have a name?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We call it "Medresa," which means "religious school."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could continue with the videotape for just a few more perhaps seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Semir Terzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I note for the record this is at the point of 13 minutes 41 seconds of this videotape. I think that's really all we need to show of the tape. I've been informed, Your Honours, from the registry officer that this videotape is actually already in evidence as Exhibit 55. So if we could get that confirmed, there would be obviously no need to tender this, this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does the Registrar confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised it is the same video, but a different time code.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can -- we can do this one of two ways, and, of course, I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands. We can tender this clip into evidence or we can tender the entire videotape into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We certainly want this tape and at least that portion which was shown today, which is eight minutes 19 seconds until 13 minutes 42 seconds, to be an exhibit; but whether it's included in the entire videotape or just this portion, we leave it to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Just the clip that was shown from eight minutes 19 seconds to 13 minutes 42 seconds will be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, earlier this morning, you told us that the Travnik Muslim Forces transformed into another unit. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber approximately when that was and what this transformation was all about?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It was the winter of 1992 and 1993. The Muslim Forces grew on to a larger formation, which was called the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And just for purposes of clarification, PW-2, if you know, did the Travnik Muslim Forces become the entire 7th Muslim Brigade or were they a component unit of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: They were the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At the time, sir, of this transformation, can you tell us approximately how many men were in the Travnik Muslim Forces, if you know?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Several hundred.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And do you know, PW-2, whether all of the members of the Travnik Muslim Forces became members of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or whether it was only some of them?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. I know that the Muslim Forces became part of the 7th Muslim Brigade. I know that there was one company from Vitez, since that's near Travnik; therefore, the area of Travnik and its surrounding areas. I don't know the details of it, though.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier this morning a few names of the leaders of the Travnik Muslim Forces, and I'd like to ask you about the role that these individuals played after this transformation. Do you know, sir, what position, if any, Asim Koricic assumed once the Travnik Muslim Forces transformed into the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Asim Koricic was our commander for a while. Later on, for a shorter period of time, he was even the commander of the 7th Muslim, but I'm not that familiar with these matters.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when you say, as reflected on page 38, line 3, "Asim Koricic was our commander for a while," what unit are you referring to when you say he "was our commander for a while"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: When we were at Karaula, at the front lines there, he was -- rather, we were under his charge, and he was charged with planning actions and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, again, sir, so that we're clear, when you were at Karaula, what unit were you assigned to? What time period and what unit are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I was part of the Muslim Forces. That's all there is to it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Following the transformation of the Muslim Forces into the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, what position did Asim Koricic hold?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I believe he became the commander of the 7th Muslim in Zenica -- or of Zenica, but I don't know the details of it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What about, sir, Mr. Ahmed Adilovic, whom you described as one of the leaders of the Travnik Muslim Forces; what position did he hold after the Travnik Muslim Forces transformed into the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: He, too, was a member of the command structure. I can't tell you anything more specific than that. He was one of the command structure, and I don't know what his function was.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: If you know, when you say "a member of the command structure," was he a member of the command structure of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade or the command structure of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, itself, the higher headquarters; do you know?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: When I joined the Muslim Forces, I believe he was, but I don't know what happened later on. I know that the army, the armija, was being formed and the situation changed. For a while, the religious influence was quite -- how shall I put it? People who were religious leaders brought more pressure to bear; and later on, the armija was -- or rather took a different course in going about its formation. I was referring to the Muslim Forces, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, Your Honours, that the witness now be shown the document which was previously marked P01027. That's P01027.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you see a document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall when and where you saw this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I saw it at the barracks of ours we referred to as "Medresa." There was one room set aside for prayers. It was there, on a shelf, that I saw several copies of this. I even read through its contents, though I can't say I recall much of it.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you recall, PW-2, whether you ever saw any other soldiers of your unit carrying or reading this book, booklet?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Probably somebody was reading it in that room. I personally did not take a copy of it, but others might have. I don't know whether somebody took a copy and carried it away.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-2, who placed the copies of this booklet in the prayer room at the Medresa in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know. It was simply there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence and it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, we will do so, but only if you would care to tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the booklet, if I can call it that, we believe speaks for itself in terms of the contents of the material contained in that -- in that booklet. The witness has indicated he doesn't recall the specifics of what's in the document, but there are certainly parts of the document that we believe are relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. But it's hard for the Chamber to admit something that we have no idea of what it is. We can't read the front page. We don't know what the contents are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is an English version of it available in e-court, but I see my learned colleague is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am opposed to the admission of this document because not a single part of it was shown to the witness, save for the cover page. I really don't know what this is about. If the Prosecutor wishes to have it admitted, then he can do this through a different witness who can comment on the contents thereof. This witness has done no such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, my colleague is looking for certain portions of this document, which we'll put to the witness in just a moment and see if he has any recollection of reading those portions. But in terms of a foundation for the admission of the document, I believe that the questions which the witness has answered are a sufficient foundation for the document to be admitted into evidence. And, of course, the issue of weight is an entirely different matter. But at the moment, perhaps. If I can just have a second while my colleague looks for the specific page, we'll put some questions to the witness concerning the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That will be helpful. We'll wait a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I've been informed that it's page 24 in English, and we're looking for the corresponding B/C/S page. If we could have page 24 in the English version brought up, please. I've been informed, Your Honours, it's page 14 in the Bosnian language version of the document. It's the page on the right-hand side. That's the left-hand side. If we can go to the right-hand side, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, I'd ask you if you could -- can you see the page on the right-hand screen or the right-hand page that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can see the page.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you take just a moment, sir, to read to yourself what's contained on this page in front of you, and then I'll ask some questions of you. Have you had an opportunity, PW-2, to read this page of the document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: A few moments ago, as reflected on page 39, lines 19 and 20, the transcript indicates that you said, "I even read through its contents, though I can't say I recall much of it." And my question to you now, sir, is: Having had the opportunity to look at this page of the document, do you recall reading this portion of the booklet on any prior occasion?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Absolutely, I don't remember the contents of this booklet. I must have read something, but I can't remember the contents. I remember some guidelines, however, that we received during preparations for combat from Semir Terzic or Ahmed Adilovic, which is equal to the first part of the text. As for the second part, no.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, that you received these guidelines that are equal to the first part of the text, what are you -- what are you referring to, specifically?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: When we were in training, with Semir Terzic in Stari Grad above Traning, he explained to us some of the rules about the Geneva Conventions which correspond to the Islamic rules. There was a signatory of those conventions, and religious rules implied them as well. Ahmed Adilovic also spoke to us, and he explained those things to us from the religious point of view.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And now, sir, with respect to the second portion or the second paragraph of this page of the document, do you recall, sir, receiving any type of instructions concerning what's contained in the second paragraph of this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We received instructions about attack, about the action. After the action, there were no such instructions. The instructions were part of the plan of action for taking certain positions or features.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, PW-2. Again, Your Honours, the Prosecution would ask this document be admitted into evidence, based upon the witness's answers and the simple fact that this document, as he indicated, was -- copies of this document were available in the Medresa in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have understood your instruction on handling documents that you gave us at the beginning of the trial, relative to long documents. The instruction said that relevant parts of long documents are presented to the witnesses, the witnesses offer their comments, and those are admitted. The Prosecutor has now been using long -- 100 pages' long documents on several occasions. He has also been using different groups of documents. He then proceeds to show the witnesses a small portion of such documents, and then has the entire document admitted as part of the evidence. Your Honours, I don't think that this is in keeping with the Rules. I believe that what needs to be or has to be admitted is only those portions that are commented on by the witness. You have been able to see what the position of the witness is. If he has been shown more of the documents, I believe the position would be different. Also, at the beginning of the trial, we had the situation when Mr. Kohlmann's books or part thereof were presented to the witness by the Defence. The Prosecutor reacted and only one page of that exhibit was admitted. We were not allowed to enter the whole book into evidence. That's why I believe that tendering exhibits into evidence in this way abborates from the instructions you that provided to us at the very start of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to the front page and the page that was shown to the witness being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. The Chamber will then admit the cover page of the document and the pages shown to the witness only. May they please be given an exhibit number. Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask at this point in time that the witness be shown the document marked P01019. That's P01019.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you now see the document in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the date of the document is that you see on the screen before you, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: 19 November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could please focus on paragraph 1.1 of this document, which is a little bit below the middle of the page under "Organisational Preparations," 1.1 (i).

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it says under "Formation"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, PW-2, whether this document corresponds approximately to the time period that you were aware of the formation of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know the date. I told you it was winter, the winter of 1992 or 1993. I don't know the date, however. I can't even give you an approximation.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you see, sir, the first -- can you read out the first sentence under "Formation"? Can you read that out loud, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: "Formation. Form a mountain brigade under the name of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade from the RBH Army armed units currently engaged on the Vlasic plateau. Form the brigade in accordance with the temporary," I can't read this, "as a mountain brigade."

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That's fine, PW-2. Can you tell us, sir, what RBH Army armed units were engaged on the Vlasic plateau in November 1992, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The portion of the document, sir, that you just read out indicates that there were RBH Army armed units engaged on the Vlasic plateau on or about 19 November 1992, and my question to you, sir, is: Do you know which RBH Army armed units were engaged on the Vlasic plateau at that time?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The 1st Krajina Brigade was engaged there, local brigades, several units, a lot of units. The territory is rather large.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that this document, P01019, be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P01019 will be admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, let me ask you, to the extent that you know, can you tell us about the structure of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade shortly after the Travnik Muslim Forces transformed into the 1st Battalion of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Could you please clarify? What structure do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Below the brigade level, to the best of your knowledge, was the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade organised into smaller units?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: There are battalions and companies and also platoons. It was organised as a classical military formation.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how many battalions the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade had at the time of the transformation, as you've described it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Possibly three, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In Zenica.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know where in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, where was that battalion headquartered, if you know?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In the town of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know the location in the town of Travnik where the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I've already told you, close to the police station. It's a different building. It's not the Medresa building.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was it the same location as the headquarters of the Travnik Muslim Forces or was it a different location?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I apologise. The command was there while the Muslim Forces were there. Later on, I don't know where the command was. I didn't follow that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Once the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was formed, what happened to the Travnik Muslim Forces?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: The Muslim Forces became the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did the Travnik -- my question actually is: Did the Travnik Muslim Forces continue to exist after the creation of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Now, PW-2, can you tell us, if you know, whether the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade consisted exclusively of Bosniak members?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: To your knowledge, sir, did the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade ever engage in combat operation with foreigners, foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes. We were often in the same field while the Muslim Forces existed and later on, although they had separate accommodation. In any case, they were separate from us, but we shared the same terrain and we engaged in the same operations.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber or can you give us some examples of locations or operations where the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade engaged in combat operation with foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It was Bijelo Bucje or the area leading towards Donji Vakuf. This is where the Arabs were billeted, or at least one group of Arabs. We also would go to that area, and we participated in the same combat operations.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber how this worked, in terms of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and the foreign fighters in the field? Can you elaborate upon -- when you say, "We participated in the same combat operations," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: After the fall of Jajce and Karaula, the Arabs, or some of them at least, because there had been a lot of groups of Arabs, one group of Arabs arrived in Bijelo Bucje. They were always there. They didn't go into town or anywhere else. This is where they stayed, where they were billeted. We, from the 1st Battalion, also arrived there on that same line of defence. The 1st Krajina Brigade also took positions there, and there was also a local unit that manned that line. When the Chetniks attacked us in that territory, we all participated in defending that territory.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber, PW-2, an indication or an approximation of the distance, the physical distance, between the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and these foreigners when you were on this line at Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: We were in one part of the village, close to one part of the front line, and they were in the other part of the village, again, close to another part of the defence line. The front line was some 200 metres away from the village. The front line was long. We were on one side of it; they were on the other side of that same line. The 1st Krajina Unit also came from time to time. It all depended. It all depended on where the direction of the attack was, and we would then all be transferred to where the brunt of the attack came from.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And during this time period that you were in Bijelo Bucje, can you give us an idea of the physical proximity that your unit was with respect to the foreign fighters, in terms of how far away from you and your unit were these foreign fighters during this time period that you were in the village?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Between 500 metres and one kilometre, but not more than one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask a question. Witness, who was ensuring the coordination between the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the groups of Arabs? Who was it, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Arabs were there all the time. That's where they were stationed, and I really don't know. The attacks happened very often. There was a lot of fighting. I can't tell you exactly. From time to time, they had some interpreters. Maybe the interpreters provided some sort of coordination. I can't really tell you. There was also some Turks there, not only Arabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just one other question. Who was commanding those units? Was it the Arabs or was it the Bosnian Muslims? Was there a one-and-only command? Was there a united command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Arabs were rather autonomous in their doings. They had their own thing, and they did their own thing. For example, I remember an Arab whose name was Abu Ubeidah, that's what they called him, Abu Ubeidah or something of the sort. He commanded the Arabs. As far as us Bosniaks were concerned, we would arrive from Travnik whenever there was an attack; in other words, we had our command in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, let's try and understand what the Judge is trying to find out. When you are on the field and fighting, surely there should be one command to coordinate the actions of the two groups, because you were fighting as allies, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the fall of the Jajce and Karaula --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Wait a minute. Just a second. The Judge is asking you not after the fall of Karaula. As you are fighting on the field, were you, the Bosniak group, fighting as allies with the Arab group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me put it this way: We fought together, which means that we launched counter-attacks in response to the Serb attacks. Who provided commands, who commanded what, I really wouldn't know. I was just a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know who was commanding the two groups; is that your short answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that Abu Ubeidah was the commander of the Arab group. We arrived in different companies or platoons, and we each had our own commanders. Who among them coordinated those activities, I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did your commanders also coordinate the activities together with the commanders of the Arabs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the coordination was. There were very frequent attacks and actions. We were running around in various directions. There were constant attacks. We had only infantry weapons. We were attacked by tanks. I really don't know what the chain of command was. I know that we were sent very often to restore the line, because the line would fall quite frequently and we were sent there to restore the lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now that I also started asking questions, can I just ask something about this document before it's removed from the screen. Before this document was placed on the screen, you talked of the formation of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Now, my question to you is: Is the 7th Muslim Brigade the same thing as the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade that you have begun to talk about since this talk document came on the screen? In the one name, there is no word "Mountain"; in the other there is the word "Mountain."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We called our brigade "The 7th Muslim Brigade." As for this name "Mountain Brigade," that's not what we called ourselves. We didn't call our brigade that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would ask now that the witness be shown the document P01043. That's P01043.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And while that's being done, sir, do you have an approximate -- or can you give us an approximation number of Arabs that you recall seeing around the area of Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. Not more than 50, let's say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask if we could please -- you'll see paragraphs 1 and 2; and under 2, there's (a) and (b). If we could please have paragraph 2(b) highlighted or enlarged on the screen, please, 2(b).

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you see the final sentence of paragraph 2(b) that makes reference to "around 60 Arabs and Turks"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I can see that it says that there are 60 Arabs and Turks who have not been included or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And you also see, under paragraph 2(a), that this document - as well as paragraph 2(b) - is referring to the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It says that there is some sort of a disposition here, but I'm not familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you see the reference, in paragraph 2(a), to 325 soldiers engaged in Bijelo Bucje that includes around 180 men?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And what was the time period, sir, to the best of your recollection, that you were engaged in the area around Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: For a long time, the front line stretched around Bijelo Bucje. I went up there quite a few times. In the meantime, we had go to the other front lines in accordance with our orders. I don't know the exact time period. From the fall of Karaula, we would go there quite often and for a long time, perhaps six months. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'd ask that P01043 be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document P01043 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 108.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be convenient?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's take a break and come back at quarter to 1:00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, can you tell us for how long you remained a member of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I was a member of the battalion until I joined the El Mujahed Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, PW-2, do you recall approximately when it was that you joined the El Mujahed Unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: After the first clashes with the Croatian Defence Council, I joined that unit.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you give us, sir, an approximate date or at least month and year when you joined the El Mujahed Unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: In the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: PW-2, at the time you joined the El Mujahed Unit, did that unit have a name or an official name, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: I know of the name of El Mujahed, or rather, El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: At the time, sir, in the summer of 1993, when you joined the El Mujahedin Unit, where was that unit headquartered?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: At Mehuric, near Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you be more specific, sir, with respect to the location of the El Mujahedin Unit in Mehuric?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: This is perhaps some 20 kilometres away from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did the location where the El Mujahedin Unit had its headquarters in Mehuric have a name? The specific location where that headquarter was based, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: It was called Mehuric. I'm not from that area originally, and it is quite possible that it had another name. I was not familiar with the territory.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you describe the location where the El Mujahedin Unit was located in Mehuric?

utterances.speaker: PW-2
utterances.text: From the center of the village, perhaps some 500 metres away from the center of the village.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And, sir, at the time you joined that unit, do you know who the commander of that El Mujahedin Unit was?
